title: Oedipus at Colonus
author: Sophocles
openingText:
[Enter the blind OEDIPUS, led by his daughter ANTIGONE.]

OEDIPUS. Antigone, child of an old blind father — tell me, what country is this? Whose city have we reached? Who today will offer even a meager handout to this wanderer? He asks for little, and gets less — but that little is enough for me. Suffering has taught me to endure, and so have the long years that have grown old alongside me, and not least my own true nobility. My daughter, if you see any resting place on common ground or beside some sacred grove, stop me and set me down. Let us find out where we have come; strangers must ask those who live here, and do whatever they are told.
about:
Old and blind, Oedipus arrives at Colonus near Athens, guided by his daughter Antigone. He seeks rest in a sacred grove, but the local people recoil when they learn his name. For Oedipus, the grove also signals that his long wandering may be coming to an end.

Ismene brings news of the struggle between his sons and of the power his final resting place may hold. Creon wants to bring him back to the borders of Thebes. Polynices asks for his support in the war against his brother. Theseus, king of Athens, promises protection. Oedipus must decide whom to trust and what he owes the family and city that drove him out.

The play brings together an old man’s dependence on others, his anger and his new religious significance. Choral songs about Colonus, old age and death interrupt the conflicts between family members and cities. At the end, a messenger describes Oedipus’s mysterious death, whose exact circumstances only Theseus knows.

angleCards.title: Making room for a stranger
angleCards.text: The chorus initially fears Oedipus, while Theseus offers protection. Follow what it takes to welcome a stranger and how the promise of sanctuary is tested.
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to examine how hospitality becomes a responsibility for another person.

angleCards.title: Guilt and intention
angleCards.text: Oedipus argues that he did not know the truth about his actions. Notice how he distinguishes what he did, what he knew and what he suffered.
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to follow Oedipus’s defense and consider the relationship between action, knowledge and guilt.

angleCards.title: Care and anger
angleCards.text: The daughters help their father, while he curses his sons. Antigone tries to persuade him to listen. Watch tenderness and refusal to forgive exist together.
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to read the family’s conversations with attention to care, betrayal and anger.

angleCards.title: The political power of a grave
angleCards.text: Oedipus is vulnerable and homeless, but his future grave has consequences for the safety of cities. Follow how Creon and Theseus respond to that power.
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to examine how religion, sanctuary and the interests of cities become connected.

cast.name: Oedipus
cast.description: Blind and old, he seeks rest after years of suffering. He defends himself against accusations of guilt, rejects Creon’s plans and puts his trust in Theseus.

cast.name: Antigone
cast.description: She guides her father, pleads his case and tries to ease the family’s conflicts. Her care for him is threatened when Creon has her seized.

cast.name: Ismene
cast.description: She reports the brothers’ struggle and the oracle’s pronouncement. She helps her father perform the rites required by the goddesses of the grove.

cast.name: Theseus
cast.description: He promises Oedipus protection and intervenes when Creon abducts the daughters. Oedipus entrusts him with the secret of his final resting place.

cast.name: Creon
cast.description: Oedipus’s brother-in-law wants to bring him to the borders of Thebes. When persuasion fails, he uses the daughters to put pressure on Oedipus.

cast.name: Polynices
cast.description: Exiled from Thebes, he seeks his father’s support before attacking the city his brother now rules. He faces his father’s anger and Antigone’s plea to abandon the war.

cast.name: Chorus
cast.description: The local old men initially reject Oedipus but later help him. They sing about the gods of Colonus, old age and the conditions of human life.

whyItMatters.title: Responsibility without full knowledge
whyItMatters.body: Oedipus’s defense makes guilt more than a question of what actually happened. His words invite reflection on how intention and ignorance affect our judgment of an action.

whyItMatters.title: Care under pressure
whyItMatters.body: The daughters’ help is practical: they guide, protect and mourn their father. At the same time, the family’s conflicts show that closeness does not guarantee reconciliation.

whyItMatters.title: An ending that remains mysterious
whyItMatters.body: The messenger can describe the preparations for Oedipus’s death but cannot explain the death itself. The play allows hope for peace to coexist with loss and uncertainty.
